intro: Toblach, Dobbiaco in Italian, is a village in the Puster valley of South Tyrol, where the road south to Cortina turns into the Dolomites. South of the village a valley of spruce and larch runs between high limestone walls, and on a gravel path through it a reader stopped under a larch so tall it rises far above the forest. They sent us its photograph in autumn, the crown gone gold against a blue sky.
meta_description: A very tall European larch beside a forest path south of Toblach in the Dolomites, sent by a reader: what it looks like and how to find it.

trees.name: The Tall Larch of the Landro Valley
trees.age_estimate: 70 to 100 years, by a reader's estimate

location.address: Forest path in the valley south of Toblach (Dobbiaco), South Tyrol

trees.story:
"Look at the photo… it's very very very tall!" wrote the reader who sent us this larch from the valley south of Toblach, in the Dolomites of South Tyrol.

They are right, and the photograph is taken to prove it. A gravel path runs into the forest under a wall of mountain, four walkers on it, and beside them a European larch climbs on a bare, straight trunk far past the spruces around it. Most of its height is clean pole; only near the top does it open into a narrow crown, and in the reader's picture that crown has turned the deep gold larches take in autumn, lit against a blue sky while the forest below is still in shade.

The larch is the one conifer of the Alps that drops its needles every winter, which is why the slopes behind it are speckled with the same orange in November. Few of them stand out like this one.

The reader puts it at 70 to 100 years old and its trunk at about 170 centimetres round. Those figures are theirs; we have not seen a measurement or a record of this tree. Our pin marks the stretch of path, not the trunk itself, so look for the tallest gold crown beside it. If you know this tree, tell us here.

Come in late October or early November, when the needles turn.
